Base directory for this skill: ~/code/video-agent-harness/.claude/worktrees/step-12-prompt-skills/server/agent/plugin/skills/summarize-video

# Summarize the video

1. Call `get_overview` if you have not already. Its chapters are the outline.
2. For each chapter, read what is said with `get_transcript` over the chapter's range. Skip this for a chapter whose overview summary already says enough and the video is long; read at least the first and last chapter.
3. If a chapter is mostly visual (little or no speech), call `inspect` once on it with "What happens here?".
4. Write the summary:
   - One or two sentences on what the video is and who is in it.
   - One bullet per chapter: `[mm:ss–mm:ss]` then what happens or is argued, in a sentence or two.
   - End with the takeaway or conclusion, cited.

Every bullet carries a citation from a tool result. If the user asked about only part of the video, summarize only that range. Keep it shorter than the video deserves rather than longer.

90.52, "time": "01:26", "speaker": "speaker_0", "text": "The way these people make money is very different than the way these people make money,"}, {"start": 91.4, "end": 93.08, "time": "01:31", "speaker": "speaker_0", "text": "He used to work on Wall Street."}, {"start": 105.02, "end": 108.34, "time": "01:45", "speaker": "speaker_0", "text": "Now he's retired and lives off his many stock market investments."}, {"start": 108.76, "end": 114.06, "time": "01:49", "speaker": "speaker_2", "text": "I own stock in companies, I mean, Berkshire Hathaway and Amazon and Apple."}, {"start": 114.66, "end": 121.1, "time": "01:55", "speaker": "speaker_0", "text": "He's a pretty typical one-percenter, except that he spends his money advocating for rich people like him to be taxed more."}, {"start": 121.5, "end": 128.919, "time": "02:02", "speaker": "speaker_2", "text": "I wanna live in a country filled with a middle class of people who can all afford to shop in our businesses."}, "They get a paycheck and pay income tax ranging from 10 to 37%."}, {"start": 137.36, "end": 143.72, "time": "02:17", "speaker": "speaker_0", "text": "But people like Morris, they make a lot of their income from investments, generally stocks and real estate."}, {"start": 144.36, "end": 152.18, "time": "02:24", "speaker": "speaker_0", "text": "These investments are taxed as capital gains, and {"start": 158.2, "end": 161.9, "time": "02:38", "speaker": "speaker_2", "text": "and my taxes on that was around $50,000."}, {"start": 162.7, "end": 169.88, "time": "02:43", "speaker": "speaker_2", "text": "But that $50,000 is far less tax than anyone who has a job making $400,000 a year would pay."}, {"start": 170.64, "end": 173.3, "time": "02:51", "speaker": "speaker_0", "text": "And most of his wealth, well, isn't even taxable."}, {"start": 173.76, "end": 182.34, "time": "02:54", "speaker": "speaker_0", "text": "People like Morris or Buffett are worth so much money because of the stock that they hold, but it's not tangible, spendable, taxable money."}, {"start": 182.76, "end": 189.82, "time": "03:03", "speaker": "speaker_2", "text": "I can look at my stock portfolio, and I can say, \"Oh, you know, I made a million dollars this year,\" but it doesn't mean I have to pay anything in taxes"}, {"start": 190.7, "end": 195.82, "time": "03:11", "speaker": "speaker_2", "text": "because our system is based on only paying taxes when you actually sell something."}, {"start": 196.22, "end": 203.32, "time": "03:16", "speaker": "speaker_0", "text": "Amazon's Jeff Bezos, the richest man in America, thanks mostly to his Amazon stock, pays almost nothing in taxes."}, {"start": 204.22, "end": 212.0, "time": "03:24", "speaker": "speaker_0", "text": "We value his worth here, but it's never taxed unless it's turned into real money when he sells the stock, and it's taxed as a capital gain."}, {"start": 213.3, "end": 219.08, "time": "03:33", "speaker": "speaker_0", "text": "This is one way billionaires are able to be technically worth so much money but pay so little in taxes."}, {"start": 219.82, "end": 225.04, "time": "03:40", "speaker": "speaker_0", "text": "Some billionaires, like Elon Musk, are able to get loans against their stocks and live off of that."}, {"start": 225.56, "end": 228.58, "time": "03:46", "speaker": "speaker_0", "text": "They don't even need to sell the stock to turn it into spendable money."}, {"start": 229.06, "end": 230.72, "time": "03:49", "speaker": "speaker_0", "text": "No sale, no taxes."}, {"start": 231.4, "end": 235.16, "time": "03:51", "speaker": "speaker_2", "text": "The fact is, if you're a billionaire, you don't need any income."}, {"start": 236.48, "end": 241.68, "time": "03:56", "speaker": "speaker_0", "text": "There's also a big loophole in capital gains taxes that the rich exploit called the stepped-up basis."}, {"start": 242.46, "end": 251.42, "time": "04:02", "speaker": "speaker_0", "text": "If, hypothetically, Warren Buffett were to sell his stock, he'd have to pay capital gains taxes based on his profit, so the cost of the stock minus the original investment."}, {"start": 252.1, "end": 262.64, "time": "04:12", "speaker": "speaker_0", "text": "But if he holds off selling his entire life, when he dies, whoever inherits the stock and then sells it would only have to pay taxes on what they earned after they inherited it,"}, {"start": 263.52, "end": 266.24, "time": "04:24", "speaker": "speaker_0", "text": "leaving all those original gains untaxed."}, {"start": 267.2, "end": 273.2, "time": "04:27", "speaker": "speaker_0", "text": "It's part of what's called buy, borrow, die, and it's one way the richest families avoid paying taxes."}, {"start": 274.02, "end": 283.92, "time": "04:34", "speaker": "speaker_0", "text": "It's this system and the fact that most taxable capital gains are going to the top 1% that lawmakers see changing the capital gains tax as an easy way to tax the rich."}, {"start": 285.22, "end": 296.72, "time": "04:45", "speaker": "speaker_0", "text": "President Biden has proposed closing that stepped-up loophole and increasing the maximum tax rate from 20% to 39.6%, but just for people making more than a million dollars a year."}, {"start": 297.3, "end": 303.56, "time": "04:57", "speaker": "speaker_0", "text": "Critics argue that it may discourage people from investing in the stock market or that current millionaires would just sell less stock."}, {"start": 304.06, "end": 310.36, "time": "05:04", "speaker": "speaker_0", "text": "But it would bring in more tax revenue from more conservative estimates of $200 billion over 10 years to double that."}, {"start": 311.26, "end": 314.98, "time": "05:11", "speaker": "speaker_0", "text": "It would also mean Buffett would pay a closer tax rate to his secretary."}, {"start": 316.08, "end": 319.4, "time": "05:16", "speaker": "speaker_0", "text": "But this pile of unrealized money still goes untaxed."}, {"start": 320.38, "end": 324.04, "time": "05:20", "speaker": "speaker_2", "text": "There's a lot of things we could do to make the system more fair."}, {"start": 324.46, "end": 326.8, "time": "05:24", "speaker": "speaker_2", "text": "We could have taxes on wealth."}, {"start": 327.18, "end": 330.44, "time": "05:27", "speaker": "speaker_2", "text": "We could have taxes on gains in the stock market."}, {"start": 331.0, "end": 341.56, "time": "05:31", "speaker": "speaker_0", "text": "Most Americans are bothered that wealthy people don't pay their fair share, and changing capital gains taxes wouldn't be the whole solution, but advocates argue it would be an easy place to start."}, {"start": 341.98, "end": 349.26, "time": "05:42", "speaker": "speaker_2", "text": "Our system is making the rich get richer and richer and richer, and everyone else just not."}, {"start": 366.5, "end": 366.82, "time": "06:06", "speaker": "speaker_2", "text": "[upbeat music]"}]}

This is a six-minute explainer on why very rich Americans often pay a lower tax rate than ordinary workers. It uses Warren Buffett as the main example and includes interviews with Morris, a retired Wall Street investor who wants people like himself to pay more tax [01:43–01:55].

- **[00:00–01:35] Buffett's tax conundrum.** Most of Buffett's wealth is in Berkshire Hathaway stock. A share was worth $19 when he took over the company in 1965 and is worth nearly $500,000 today, and he owns about 240,000 shares [00:27–00:41]. He pays a lower tax rate than his secretary and calls that "outrageous" [00:44–00:53]. The reason is that her salary is taxed as income, while his money comes from selling stock, which is taxed as capital gains at nearly half the rate [00:57]. Over the past 40 years, the after-tax income of the richest has grown more than 400%, compared with 50% for the middle class [01:11].
- **[01:35–03:55] Income tax vs. capital gains.** Pay from a job is taxed at 10–37%, but long-term stock gains are taxed at no more than 20% [02:12–02:24]. Morris says he sold $400,000 of stock and paid about $50,000 in tax, far less than someone earning $400,000 from a job would pay [02:33–02:43]. Stock that hasn't been sold isn't taxed at all, which is why Jeff Bezos pays almost nothing [03:03–03:24]. Billionaires like Elon Musk can also borrow against their shares and live on the loans: "No sale, no taxes" [03:40–03:49].
- **[03:55–04:44] "Buy, borrow, die."** Under a rule called "stepped-up basis," someone who inherits stock is only taxed on gains made after they inherit it. Everything the stock gained during the original owner's lifetime is never taxed [03:56–04:27].
- **[04:44–06:07] Proposed reforms.** President Biden proposed ending stepped-up basis and raising the top capital gains rate from 20% to 39.6% for people earning over $1 million a year [04:45]. Critics say this could discourage investing [04:57]. Estimates of the extra revenue run from $200 billion to about double that over 10 years [05:04]. Even then, stock that hasn't been sold would still go untaxed [05:16], so Morris suggests wealth taxes or taxing stock market gains as they happen [05:20–05:27].

**Takeaway:** Changing capital gains taxes wouldn't fix everything, but supporters say it's an easy place to start [05:31]. Morris closes with: "Our system is making the rich get richer and richer… and everyone else just not" [05:42].
